title: 1871's river bridges meet their streets, and Lake Park is open
items: Each river bridge now carries its own street across, level with the road at both banks, instead of running into buildings at an angle.
The bridges are centre-pivot swing bridges, with a tower over the round pier, iron rods to the ends, a timber deck and railed walks.
The white square you saw on the State Street bridge at night is gone.
Corner stores on Washington and Clark streets no longer stand out over the sidewalk and street.
The lakefront east of Michigan Avenue, from Randolph to Twelfth Street, is Lake Park again, with no houses on it.
Buildings seen from far off keep their brick and paint instead of turning bright blue.
